name: Business Email Compromise and Invoice Redirection
description: Criminals compromise or spoof email accounts to impersonate executives or suppliers and redirect payments to accounts they control. Typical outcomes are urgent wire requests or changed bank details on genuine invoices.

sources.text: FinCEN, Updated Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes Targeting Vulnerable Business Processes, FIN-2019-A005 (2019)
FBI IC3, Business E-Mail Compromise: The $55 Billion Scam (PSA I-091124-PSA, 2024)
UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)

exposure.rationale: Business payment redirection via email compromise, mostly wires.

indicators.name: Change of beneficiary bank details close to a payment
indicators.canon: Change of beneficiary bank details close to a payment
indicators.desc: Victim-side: supplier payment details are altered shortly before an invoice is due, via email or portal.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: supplier payment details are altered shortly before an invoice is due, via email or portal.
refs: FinCEN, Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes (2019)

indicators.name: Urgent confidential payment request from a senior executive
indicators.canon: Urgent payment instruction or payment-detail change outside normal process
indicators.desc: Staff receive urgent, confidential requests, or changes to beneficiary details, directing payment to a new beneficiary outside normal workflow.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: finance staff receive a request, often outside normal workflow, to wire funds quickly and not discuss it.
refs: FinCEN, Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes (2019)

indicators.name: Lookalike or recently registered sender domain
indicators.canon: Lookalike or recently registered sender domain
indicators.desc: Spoofed email domain or reply-to differs subtly from the genuine counterparty.
indicators.ctx: Spoofed email domain or reply-to differs subtly from the genuine counterparty.
refs: FinCEN, Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes (2019)

indicators.name: First payment to a new beneficiary in a different jurisdiction
indicators.canon: First payment to a new beneficiary in a different jurisdiction
indicators.desc: Victim-side: payment to a new account, often foreign, unrelated to the supplier's usual country.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: payment to a new account, often foreign, unrelated to the supplier's usual country.
refs: FinCEN, Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes (2019)

indicators.name: Business account receives funds then moves them offshore or to crypto quickly
indicators.canon: Rapid movement offshore or to crypto after receipt
indicators.desc: Incoming funds are quickly sent abroad or converted to virtual assets soon after being credited.
indicators.ctx: Mule-side: a recipient account (often newly opened or a shell) forwards BEC proceeds within hours.
refs: FinCEN, Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes (2019)

indicators.name: Invoice amount or format differs from prior invoices
indicators.canon: Invoice amount or format differs from prior invoices
indicators.desc: Victim-side: genuine-looking invoice has altered layout, round figures or inconsistent references.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: genuine-looking invoice has altered layout, round figures or inconsistent references.
refs: FinCEN, Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes (2019)

indicators.name: Payment initiated outside normal approval chain
indicators.canon: Payment initiated outside normal approval chain
indicators.desc: bypass of the usual purchase order or approval, or approver working remotely at odd hours.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: bypass of the usual purchase order or approval, or approver working remotely at odd hours.
refs: FinCEN, Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes (2019)

indicators.name: Shell or newly formed company receiving corporate payments
indicators.canon: Shell entity with no operating footprint
indicators.desc: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.
indicators.ctx: Mule-side: beneficiary has little trading footprint, a virtual office or recent incorporation.
refs: FinCEN, Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes (2019)

indicators.name: Corporate login from unusual location or after mailbox rule change
indicators.canon: Corporate login from unusual location or after mailbox rule change
indicators.desc: mailbox forwarding rules and unfamiliar logins precede payment fraud.
indicators.ctx: Compromise indicator: mailbox forwarding rules and unfamiliar logins precede payment fraud.
